purpose: Phenazopyridine helps relieve the burning, pain, and discomfort that comes with a urinary tract infection (UTI) or bladder irritation. It soothes the lining of your urinary tract so you feel more comfortable when you urinate. It is a pain reliever only — it does NOT treat or cure the infection itself.
how_it_works: This medicine works by coating and soothing the irritated lining of your bladder and urinary tract, kind of like a numbing agent for that area. It is excreted through your urine, so it acts right where the pain and irritation are happening. Think of it as a local pain reliever that goes directly to the source of your discomfort.
common_side_effects: Your urine will turn bright orange or reddish — this is completely normal and expected, so do not be alarmed! It can stain your underwear or contact lenses, so be careful. You may also experience headache, upset stomach, or dizziness in some cases.
warnings: This medication is only for short-term use, usually no more than 2 days. It does NOT kill bacteria, so if you have a UTI you still need an antibiotic from your doctor. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease or liver problems before taking this. Stop taking it and call your doctor if your skin or eyes turn yellow, as this could be a sign of a serious problem.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 95 mg to 200 mg taken by mouth 3 times a day, after meals, for up to 2 days. Always follow the directions on the package or your doctor's instructions. Do not take it for more than 2 days unless your doctor specifically tells you to.
